meta.note: figmaStatus reflects what is ACTUALLY built in the Figma library. Components with figmaStatus 'proposed' are specified here but NOT yet drawn in Figma, so do not claim they exist. codeName/props are the proposed API; runtime stack is provisional (see STORYBOOK.md). WHITE-LABEL: Envision serves many builder brands. No component may assume a brand color — consume semantic roles (background/brand, content/on-brand), never color/primary/* directly, and never pair a fixed content color with a brand surface. Themeable surface and invariants: SYSTEM_SPEC §9.

componentTaxonomy.note: Category axis mirrors the section dividers in the Figma library, so a component sits in the same place in both. Status & Progress is its own section again, and Table returns to Data Display. The prior axis is preserved per component as categoryPrevious.
componentTaxonomy.internal: Internal subcomponents carry `category: null` and `public: false`. They are never members of the seven public categories.
componentTaxonomy.unspecified: Entries with `specified: false` are inventory records for components that exist in the Figma library but have no registry specification yet. They carry identity and category only.
componentTaxonomy.separateFrom: Component taxonomy is independent of the token taxonomy and of `architecture` (atomic composition level). A component's category has no bearing on its token namespace.

components.content: Do not flatten complex samples to hex when texture fidelity needed.
components.whenToUse: Anywhere a material is chosen: the rail’s swatch grids, a Selection Tray, a Finish Group. Chip for paint, wood and stone, whose sample is a flat color or texture. Sphere for metal finishes such as hardware and faucets, whose sample is a rendered material that needs curvature to read.
components.whenNotToUse: Do not use a chip for a metal finish or a sphere for a paint color: the shape is how a reader tells the two apart. Do not flatten a textured sample to a hex value when the texture is what is being chosen.
components.anatomyNote: A sample with a selection ring, and an optional label beneath. The fill is product data, an image, texture or color set per instance, never a token: the swatch shows the material itself.
behavior: Selection is a ring, never color alone, because the fill is product data and can be any color.
A swatch does not reorder when it is chosen. Its position in a grid is the catalog’s order, not a record of what was picked.

behavior: Curated swatches hold their positions. Choosing one selects it where it already sits: a swatch that jumps to the front moves every other swatch under the pointer and makes the row impossible to scan the same way twice.
The one exception is a color chosen from the picker that is not in the curated set. It has nowhere to sit, so it prepends as the first tile, pushes the rest over, and drops the last curated swatch.
The row is capped at eleven swatches plus the opener, which opens the full picker.
One tray is open at a time; opening another dismisses the current one.

components.purpose: The full-bleed 3D canvas the Design Center is built around, hosting the live kitchen model.
components.whenToUse: As the Design Center’s canvas region. One per view; the rail and trays sit over it.
components.whenNotToUse: Not for a still image of a room. If the model is not interactive, that is a Thumbnail or an image, not a viewport.
components.anatomyNote: A canvas filling its region, with a preloader over it while the first assets download and the camera framing driven by whichever tray is open.
behavior: The preloader appears only while the initial assets are downloading, and its bar is driven by real bytes: never a timed or decorative animation.
The scene mounts only once assets are cached, and the bar reaches 100% only when the scene has actually rendered. If everything is cached, the model shows immediately with no preloader.
Opening a tray reframes the camera to that subject: countertop, backsplash, hardware or faucet.
Covered by another tab, the render loop idles rather than unmounting, so the GPU context and buffers survive for an instant return.

props.name: active
props.note: false idles the render loop without unmounting

components.a11y: A canvas cannot be read by assistive technology, so every choice it visualises must also be available as text in the rail. The viewport is a preview, never the only place a selection is stated.
components.responsive: Fills its region. The rail and trays overlay it rather than shrinking it.

components.purpose: The full wall-color library, opened from the rail to browse, search and apply any curated color.
components.anatomyNote: Header with the title, search and close. Sidebar of color families. Content with the count, a sort control and a five-column swatch grid. Footer with Save Color and Select This Color.
components.whenToUse: When the eleven curated chips in the rail are not enough. The opener beside them is what brings it up.
components.whenNotToUse: Not for a short set of options that fits in the rail, and not bottom-anchored like a Selection Tray: this is a centered overlay because browsing a library is a task of its own.
behavior: The grid is ordered by value first, then intensity, then hue, so it reads as a gradient rather than as the order the catalog was authored in. Value is banded rather than compared exactly, because a difference the eye cannot see should not outrank hue.
Select This Color is disabled until a color is chosen.
Clicking a swatch live-previews it on the model. Select This Color commits and closes; Save Color stores it without closing.
Esc or the close button dismisses and reverts the preview.
Search filters within the active category, and choosing a category resets the grid.
A chosen library color becomes the first chip in the rail, since it has no curated position of its own.
components.a11y: Focus is trapped while open, and Esc or close dismisses it, reverting the preview. Search is a labeled input. The selected swatch shows a check and a ring, not color alone. The category list is keyboard-navigable.
components.content: Swatch cells carry the color name and its catalog code. Both come from the catalog, so neither is a token or a translation string. Ordering is computed in OKLCH: HSL lightness is a channel average, so it would place a near-white and a near-black side by side.

components.purpose: The selectable material preview used inside every picker tile and rail card.
components.anatomyNote: A fixed-ratio preview with a selection ring. Placeholder art ships in the component; the real material image overrides the fill per instance. It never adds a label itself.
components.a11y: Hover shows a faint ring and selection a solid one, never color alone. Keyboard focusable with a visible focus ring; unavailable materials are dimmed and non-interactive.
components.whenToUse: Inside a picker tile or rail card that needs a selectable material preview.
components.whenNotToUse: On its own. It never carries a label; the name and price live on the parent tile or card. For a non-selectable image, use Thumbnail.

components.a11y: Always provide an accessible name, the user’s full name, even though only initials are shown. Initials meet 3:1 contrast on the neutral fill. When interactive, guarantee a hit area of at least 40px around the 28 to 34px circle.
